items.note: Source: Cenovia Park home page, read 21 Oct 2026. It says 6100 places, 16 public car parks, 173 street machines and describes Cenovia Park as the operator of the Le Mans conurbation. It does NOT say 3.4 million vehicles in 2025: it says '3,5 M de vehicules passes par Cenovia chaque annee' (undated). The 3.4 million (2025) figure is on cenovia.fr (the item 8 source), not here. The page also does not say the city and the metropole entrusted the car parks to Cenovia Park; that is on the city's stationnement page (item 1 source) and names only the Ville du Mans, not the metropole. The 1.92 million (2022) figure is on the city page and is right. Live page, so date 2026-10 is right.
items.corrected_text: Cénovia Park describes itself as the parking operator of the Le Mans conurbation. Its home page (read on 21 October 2026) shows about 6,100 car-park spaces, 16 public car parks and 173 on-street ticket machines, and says 3.5 million vehicles pass through Cénovia each year (the figure is not dated; Cénovia's group site gives 3.4 million vehicles in its car parks in 2025). The city's parking page says the Ville du Mans entrusted the underground car parks and paid on-street parking to Cénovia Park, and cites 1.92 million drivers using the city's paid car parks in 2022.

items.note: City page read through the site's public JSON endpoint (www.lemans.fr/api/..., HTTP 200, no challenge, no redirect; only a PHPSESSID session cookie). Text matches: 3638 car-park places plus 2123 paid on-street places; sign at each entrance showing free places; République 774, Jacobins 388, Quinconces 610 underground and 350 above ground, Filles-Dieu 165, Médiathèque 240, Rabelais 92, Halles 240, Gare-Sud 269, Novaxis 42, Palais-des-Congrès 380, Gare-Nord 88 (they sum to 3638). Page edit stamp 26 May 2025. Note the page says '12 parkings' but lists 11 names (Quinconces counted twice). Operator's live figures differ (e.g. Halles 162, Quinconces P1 398, Filles Dieu 164).

FPS amounts match the page (edit stamp 10 Jun 2025): fixed at 30 euros, reduced to 20 euros if paid within three days, 50 euros more (80 total) if nothing paid within three months; table shows 20 / 30 / 80. But the page does not say FPS can be paid 'at the ticket machine in cash or by card'. The '3 euros maximum' line is a tip for using the parking meter ('N'insérez jamais plus de 3 euros'), not about paying an FPS; FPS payment is explained in a separate 'fiche-démarche' that this page links to.
items.corrected_text: On-street parking: the post-parking charge (FPS) in Le Mans is 30 euros, reduced to 20 euros if paid within three days; if nothing is paid within three months a further 50 euros is due, making 80 euros in total (city page, edit stamp June 2025). The same page advises meter users never to insert more than 3 euros, the maximum amount allowed.

items.note: Cenovia voirie page read on 21 Oct 2026 (live). Hours match for Zones 1, 2 and 3: paid 9h-12h30 and 14h-19h Monday to Saturday, free Sundays and public holidays. Street tariff tables: most streets 15 min 0.50, 30 min 1.00, 45 min 1.50, 1h 2.50, 1h30 3.00, then '2h 30,00 EUR'; 58 other streets 30 min 0.50, 1h 1.00, 1h30 1.50, 2h 2.00, then '2h30 30,00 EUR'. Not supported: 'in the centre' (the page lists addresses by street, no centre label) and that 30 euros is 'the amount beyond the maximum stay' (the tables just show 30 euros in the row after the last paid duration, with no label; it equals the FPS amount but the page does not say so).
items.corrected_text: On-street parking is paid 9am-12:30pm and 2pm-7pm Monday to Saturday and free on Sundays and public holidays (operator page read on 21 October 2026). On most listed streets the tariff table runs 0.50 euros for 15 minutes, 1 euro for 30 minutes, 1.50 euros for 45 minutes, 2.50 euros for one hour and 3 euros for 1.5 hours; on some other streets it is 0.50 euros per 30 minutes up to 2 hours. The tables show 30 euros in the row after the longest paid duration (2 hours, or 2.5 hours on the other streets) without saying what it is.

items.note: République page read 21 Oct 2026: 15 min free, 30 min 1.00, 1h 1.50, 4h 7.50, 12h 15.00 (7h-19h), 1 euro 19h-7h. I also read the Jacobins and Quinconces aérien P1 pages: identical scale. Quinconces P2 page: 1h free, 1h30 1.00, 1h45 1.50, 2h-4h 2.00, 12h 14.00, 1 euro evening; car park free 7h-14h (Sunday market) and Sunday/holiday opening 7h-14h. Only the République claim is on the cited URL; the others are on sibling pages of the same operator, all matching. Contradiction to note: ICI Maine (item 6) says first 30 minutes free in all car parks, but République/Jacobins/Quinconces P1 show only 15 minutes free (30 min costs 1 euro); the 30-minute free applies at Halles, Gare Nord and Gare Sud P1.

Gare Nord page (and Gare Sud P1 page, identical): first 30 min free, 45 min 1.00, 1h 2.00 ... 4h 14.00, 12h 46.00 (7h-21h), 1 euro night. Gare Sud P2 page: 269 places; 15 min free, 30 min 1.00, 1h 1.50, 4h 7.50, 12h 15.00; weekend package 26.00 (Friday 19h to Monday 7h); holiday packages 42 / 63 / 79 euros; booking delay 8 days. 'much cheaper' is the researcher's comparison and fair. Gare Sud P2 and Gare Sud P1 are on sibling pages, not the cited URL, but all match.

Article on ici.fr (francebleu.fr link redirects there), datePublished 2025-11-17, read in full. Supported: about 150 posters on bus shelters promoting existing offers; first half hour free in all Le Mans car parks; Quinconces underground first hour free and 4 hours for 2 euros; 'shopping + soiree' 3 euros from 15h; 1 euro 19h-7h in city-centre car parks; councillor Blandine Affagard says Le Mans is the cheapest western French city for centre parking (compared with Tours, Angers, Nantes); Cenovia director Loic Sevin says Quinconces is under-used. Overstated: shopkeepers were split, not united: one blamed roadworks, one said spending power rather than access is the problem, one said car parks are poorly signposted. Also the campaign is described as the city's (with Cenovia backing it). Caution: 'first half hour free in all car parks' is the article's claim; operator pages in Oct 2026 show only 15 minutes free at République, Jacobins and Quinconces P1.
items.corrected_text: ICI Maine reported on 17 November 2025 that the city ran a poster campaign (about 150 posters at bus shelters), backed by Cénovia, for existing offers: first 30 minutes free in all car parks, first hour free and 4 hours for 2 euros at the underground Quinconces car park, a 'shopping + evening' offer of 3 euros from 3pm, and 1 euro from 7pm to 7am in city-centre car parks. A municipal councillor said Le Mans is the cheapest city in western France for centre parking, ahead of Tours, Angers or Nantes; Cénovia's director general said Quinconces is under-used. Shopkeepers were divided: one blamed roadworks for weak trade, one said spending power rather than access is the problem, and one said the car parks are poorly signposted.

items.note: City page via public JSON endpoint (edit stamp 24 Sep 2026). Supported: Cité Plantagenêt is a regulated pedestrian zone for traffic and parking; two badges max per household; delivery ticket for 30 minutes max between 5h and 11h; 5000 passages a week (described as vehicles entering the pedestrian area each week, undated); Place d'Alger protected 22h-6h every day, only residents may drive in. But the badge / delivery-ticket / two-badge rules are listed under the general central pedestrian area (entry bollards) while the Cité Plantagenêt itself uses 'macarons' (Résident, Circulation) - the draft puts them all under the Cité. The page says Place d'Alger is a protected perimeter; 'closed to non-residents' is a fair paraphrase.
items.corrected_text: Car traffic is regulated in the Cité Plantagenêt and on the central pedestrian plateau, and only residents and authorised users may enter (city page, last edited September 2026). In the central pedestrian area, residents and traders with a badge (a maximum of two badges per household), delivery drivers with a 'Livraison' ticket for up to 30 minutes between 5am and 11am, and other authorised users may enter. The Cité Plantagenêt itself is regulated for both traffic and parking, with access only for holders of a resident or circulation permit (macaron). The page gives about 5,000 vehicle entries a week into the pedestrian area (undated figure), and Place d'Alger has a protected perimeter from 10pm to 6am every day in which only residents may drive.

items.note: Cenovia group page read 21 Oct 2026. Supported on the cited page: Cenovia Park launched Le Mans Parkings Partages (LMP2) in 2024, an open platform for letting and renting private spaces, to add supply for residents of the metropolis; 'stationnement en temps reel' is listed as a service. NOT on the cited page: bookings around the station / city centre / 24 Heures (that is on lemansparkingspartages.fr), bike parking at 10 euros a year (cenoviapark.fr/parking-a-velo says République, Halles, Rabelais, with the header also naming Hôpital P4), live free-space counts on the home page (true on cenoviapark.fr home, a different site), and PayByPhone / EasyPark (not found on any page I read, including cenoviapark.fr/voirie, which only has a heading 'Paiement mobile, forfait FPS...'). The PayByPhone/EasyPark claim is unsupported.
items.corrected_text: Cénovia Park launched Le Mans Parkings Partagés in 2024 (page read on 21 October 2026), an open platform for renting and letting private parking spaces, to add supply for residents of the Le Mans metropolis; the page also lists real-time parking information among its services.

items.note: Page read 21 Oct 2026. Header: '14 bornes en services au sein de 5 parkings'; body: 'deployees sur 6 parkings majeurs'; list 4 République, 2 Jacobins, 4 Quinconces P2, 2 Médiathèque, 2 Gare Sud P2 (=14, five car parks); badge readers; redirects to E Totem for the service. The 5-versus-6 inconsistency is correct as stated.

Metropole page via public JSON endpoint (page edit stamp 11 Sep 2026): 'sur les 130000 vehicules legers presents sur le territoire, 4000 sont electriques ... actuellement 400 points de charge mais ce besoin est estime a 2000 en 2035'; with a public service, objective of a network of 1000 charge points by 2035. The 'today' figures are undated on the page. Page does not say 'public' charge points for the 400 (it just says points de charge).

Metropole transport page via public JSON endpoint (edit stamp 14 Sep 2026): two park-and-ride sites, Antarès and Université-Bartholdi; 'L'abonnement à la Setram inclut le stationnement dans les parkings-relais'. The Bartholdi pricing (3.50 euros per day, travel for up to four occupants, 450 spaces, 22 euro monthly) is NOT on this page. I confirmed it separately on the operator's pages: cenoviapark.fr/parkings/parking-bartholdi/ (450 places; Park & Tram P+R ticket 3.50 euros valid for the day, per car, unlimited Setram travel, tickets for up to 4 occupants collected at the machine) and the cenoviapark.fr home page banner (22 euros per month subscription at Bartholdi), read 21 Oct 2026. So the claim is true but sourced from a different URL.
items.corrected_text: Two park-and-ride sites serve the tram network, Antarès and Université-Bartholdi, and a Setram season ticket includes parking in them (Le Mans Métropole page, last edited September 2026).

items.note: Metropole 'Le projet' page via public JSON endpoint (edit stamp 8 Sep 2026). Supported: three busiest bus lines C4, C5, C6; 13 km of dedicated lanes 'vont etre crees' (future); C4 serves the station in both directions; Boulevard Nicolas-Cugnot to go from 2x2 lanes at 70 km/h to an urban boulevard 2x1 at 50 km/h ('deviendra' - future). NOT on this page: works started autumn 2024 and phased deliveries Dec 2025 - Nov 2026 (these are on the sibling page 'Les travaux des Chronolignes', which says works began at the rentrée 2024 for staggered deliveries between December 2025 and November 2026 and that dates are provisional, edit stamp 14 Sep 2026), and the C4 entering service on 31 August 2026 / city news of 7 September 2026 (not on the page; a web search shows radio coverage of this but I did not open it, so treat as unconfirmed).
items.corrected_text: The Chronolignes programme rebuilds the three busiest bus lines, C4, C5 and C6, with 13 km of dedicated lanes still to be created (Le Mans Métropole project page, last edited September 2026). The C4 route is changed slightly so that it serves the railway station in both directions. The plan also turns Boulevard Nicolas-Cugnot from a two-by-two-lane 70 km/h ring road into a two-by-one-lane 50 km/h urban boulevard.
items.unconfirmed_text: A web search result says the C4 Chronoligne entered service on Monday 31 August 2026, replacing bus line 4; the first Chronoligne to open. Not read on the cited page.
items.unconfirmed_reason: The project page does not give the opening date; the source for the 31 August 2026 start was not opened and a search snippet is not confirmation. The works timetable (autumn 2024 start, staggered deliveries December 2025 to November 2026, provisional dates) is on a sibling page, not the cited one.

items.note: City news item via public JSON endpoint (news date 10 Jun 2026; no challenge or redirect). Text: first lengthened tram unit 'La Chapelle Saint-Aubin' carried first passengers Wednesday 10 June, ahead of the 24 Heures; length from 32 m to 44 m; capacity to rise 40% progressively, 296 passengers per unit versus 211 now; the 33 other units to be lengthened at a forecast two a month, build-up by end 2027; Stéphane Le Foll quote that major events at Stade Marie-Marvingt, Antarès Arena and the circuit could not be handled without the tram; aim to return to pre-Covid ridership of around 30 million travellers a year. The 33 further units and the end-2027 date are forecasts, and the draft words them as plans. Fine.

ACO access page read 21 Oct 2026 (no challenge). T1 towards Antarès - Stade Marie Marvingt to the terminus, 200 m from the Porte Est; dense traffic expected; park-and-ride lots at motorway exits with frequent shuttles; train, car-sharing and bike-parking details 'will be shared soon / in the coming months'. The page gives no event date and no edition year, so the draft rightly says it is undated and no event dates are given.

Cenovia article (published 12 Oct 2026, modified 13 Oct 2026) says the operational amendment to the Projet Partenarial d'Aménagement was signed 'le 23 septembre' at the Préfecture de la Sarthe (year implied by the 12 Oct 2026 publication date). 12 hectares of former military land near the centre; 700+ homes, a school, shops, 'un parking silo'; first land sales from end 2027, first demolitions 2028; at least ten years. All worded as planned in the draft. The page gives no capacity for the parking silo. The page date is 12 Oct 2026; the draft's 2026-09-23 is the signing date.

data.gouv.fr dataset page read 21 Oct 2026 (also the data.gouv API): 'Stationnement cyclable 2026 (Le Mans Métropole)', 825 lignes with XY coordinates, Etalab cycle-parking schema, ODbL, last update 16 July 2026. NOT right: the Setram GTFS feed is published by the organisation SETRAM, not Le Mans Métropole, and is not on the cited page. Le Mans Métropole's organisation on data.gouv.fr has 4 datasets (cycle facilities, cycle parking 2026, and two procurement declarations). My own searches of the data.gouv API ('Le Mans parking', 'stationnement', 'Cénovia') found no car-park availability or on-street dataset, consistent with the draft's negative, but that is a search result not a page statement. Live page: date should be 2026-10.
items.corrected_text: Le Mans Métropole's open-data page on data.gouv.fr (read on 21 October 2026) lists a 2026 cycle-parking dataset of 825 rows with coordinates, last updated 16 July 2026, under the ODbL licence.

items.note: Operator notice (published 30 Jun 2026, modified 17 Aug 2026 per page metadata) says Halles closed 16 July to 20 September inclusive for improvement and accessibility works, reopening planned 21 September; subscribers use Médiathèque; hourly customers use Médiathèque and République; the page text gives no year (metadata indicates 2026). Operator's car park page: 162 car places; city page: 240. NOT right: the draft says the home page showed 82 free spaces for Halles. When I read the home page on 21 Oct 2026 (twice) it showed 'Fermé' for Les Halles (capacity 162), and Médiathèque 80 free; Halles detail page also showed 'Fermé'. So the status was consistent (closed) but a month past the announced 21 September reopening, with no explanation; the '82 free' reading looks like a misreading of the neighbouring Médiathèque figure (80).
items.corrected_text: Cénovia Park announced that its Halles car park would be closed from 16 July to 20 September (the notice text gives no year; the page metadata dates it 2026) for improvement and accessibility works, with reopening planned for 21 September and subscribers redirected to the Médiathèque car park. The operator lists 162 spaces for Halles and the city's page lists 240. On 21 October 2026 both the Halles page and the operator's home page still showed the car park as 'Fermé', a month after the planned reopening, with no explanation on the pages read.

corrected_summary: Le Mans's underground car parks and paid on-street parking are run by Cénovia Park, to which the city says it entrusted them; the operator reports about 6,100 spaces, 16 public car parks and 173 street ticket machines, and the city lists 3,638 car-park spaces plus 2,123 paid on-street spaces on a page last edited in May 2025. On-street parking is paid 9am-12:30pm and 2pm-7pm Monday to Saturday and free on Sundays and holidays. A missed payment costs a post-parking charge of 30 euros, 20 euros if paid within three days and 80 euros in total after three months. Car-park tariffs vary by site: at République, Jacobins and Quinconces P1 the first 15 minutes are free, then 1 euro to 30 minutes, 1.50 euros for the first hour and 7.50 euros for four hours; the underground Quinconces P2 gives the first hour free and four hours for 2 euros; the station car parks Gare Nord and Gare Sud P1 are much steeper (14 euros for four hours) while Gare Sud P2 is cheaper (7.50 euros for four hours). A November 2025 local radio report said the city promoted existing offers, with a councillor saying Le Mans is the cheapest western French city for centre parking, Cénovia saying Quinconces is under-used, and shopkeepers divided over the causes of weak trade (roadworks, spending power, signposting). The Cité Plantagenêt and the central pedestrian plateau are access-controlled. The operator lists 14 electric-vehicle charge points in five city-centre car parks, and the metropole's climate page counts about 400 charge points against a target of 1,000 by 2035. Park-and-ride sites at Antarès and Université-Bartholdi are included in Setram season tickets. The metropole's Chronolignes project plans 13 km of dedicated bus lanes on three lines and a calmer Boulevard Nicolas-Cugnot; a lengthened tram unit entered service on 10 June 2026 with the rest planned to follow by end 2027. The Arsenal-Marais redevelopment (700+ homes and a multi-storey car park) is a long-term plan, with land sales from end 2027. The Halles car park was announced closed from 16 July to 20 September 2026 and still showed as closed on 21 October 2026. Open data is thin: Le Mans Métropole publishes a cycle-parking dataset but no car-park availability dataset was found on data.gouv.fr.
